figures.caption: A quarter-round completes in registers before publishing its four words.
figures.alt: Four annotated details show t0 through t3 after the final scalar quarter-round group and all four separated caller words before any store. The result low words are ea2a92f4, cb1cf8ce, 4581472e and 5881c4bb; memory still contains the four input values and a5 gaps.

figures.caption: One scalar double-round transforms the working copy while preserving the input.
figures.alt: Six annotated details show the first after_scalar_call8 visit. The remaining double-round count s2 is ten because the decrement has not executed. All sixteen input words remain unchanged. The sixteen working words contain the first column round followed by the first diagonal round, before feed-forward.

figures.caption: Lane selection prepares the diagonal quarter-rounds.
figures.alt: Five annotated details at after_msa_select show all four working row vectors, four preserved original row vectors and all sixteen input words. Destination lane zero corresponds to column-round state positions zero, five, ten and fifteen. The hexadecimal whole-vector display places lane zero on the right.

figures.caption: A sixty-five-byte message consumes one full block and one byte of the next.
figures.alt: Six annotated details at main_done show status zero, all sixty-five output bytes and the untouched destination suffix. The first sixty-four bytes use counter one and the last uses counter two. The original counter, nonce and input bytes remain unchanged; caller status has not yet been stored.
